section: Signature Microsoft Teams Rooms: why standardized AV furniture and power matter for users and IT
body:
This AVI-SPL blog post by Mathew DeFreitas, dated July 2025, argues that the furniture, mounting and power in a Signature Microsoft Teams Room should be standardized just like the AV. It helps a consultant explain why room infrastructure matters when a customer standardizes on these rooms.

**What Signature Microsoft Teams Rooms are, per the post**
- A standardized room design for hybrid collaboration, with meetings that start at one touch, displays in 21:9 format, and furniture customized for AV to suit each room design.
- Microsoft works with Legrand AV and other certified technology partners so the rooms can be replicated and scaled easily.
- Keeping AV, furniture and power consistent makes everything simpler, from setup through to IT support.
- In-room and remote participants both value the meeting equity these rooms provide.
- Once people in one office see the approach working, adoption by other teams becomes easier, and the consistent layout lets IT deploy and support the rooms with confidence.

**Benefits for users**
- When every room has the same mounts, furniture, outlets and panels and behaves the same way, people settle in and focus more easily.
- Setup time falls. Users stop worrying about startup, finding outlets or finding cables to share content, so attention goes to collaboration and business outcomes.
- In-room attendees see remote colleagues clearly through Microsoft's Front Row meeting layout. Virtual participants get consistent, high-quality audio and video and speaker attribution.

**Benefits for IT**
- Mixing furniture and power systems from many brands gives each site its own style but creates problems, maintenance among them.
- Multiple vendors add complexity: warranties conflict, lead times slip, and a discontinued part can force IT to redesign the space.
- Buying furniture and power from the smallest possible number of trusted providers makes deployment simpler, makes replacement easier and supports global scale.
- The post admits this is hard to do with a single manufacturer, because some specialize in certain solutions and some tools are not available in every region.
- It presents Legrand AV, which it calls a global leader in AV/UC infrastructure, as making that job much easier.

**When to use this**
Use it when a customer standardizing on Signature Microsoft Teams Rooms asks why furniture and power need to be specified consistently, or how to reduce vendor sprawl across regions.

**Not stated in this source**: prices, lead times or figures for the productivity gains.
